html:
The March Days were three days of fighting in Baku at the end of March 1918, in which Bolshevik and Armenian forces killed thousands of Azerbaijani and other Muslim residents of the city.

After the Russian Revolution, the Baku Commune led by Stepan Shaumyan held the city. A clash over a Muslim regiment grew into street fighting, and Armenian Dashnak units turned on Muslim quarters. Estimates of the dead run to about 12,000. In September 1918 the Ottoman led Army of Islam took Baku for the Azerbaijan Democratic Republic, and Azerbaijani irregulars killed thousands of Armenians in return. The two massacres set a pattern of violence between the nations that returned in the Karabakh wars.
sum: The March Days were three days of fighting in Baku at the end of March 1918, in which Bolshevik and Armenian forces killed thousands of Azerbaijani and other Muslim residents of the city.
